subproblem.title: Closure theorem in degree d + 1 from CL(d) and BR(d) by localization (Simon 8.3(1))
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT) and (VO). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the parent node's dependency theorems: (REP) and (IMC) are the first and second conjuncts of the frozen statement of dimred_mbl_current_foundations, (MR) is the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (the first conjunct of its conclusion: M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every IMRep R of T in an open U and every open W; its support identity is not needed), and (SL), (DT), (VO) are the frozen statements of dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds, dimred_mbl_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support. They are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear as hypotheses of the Lean statement ((REP), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) verbatim, (MR) as the stated mass identity) and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. CL(d) denotes: for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), T is integer multiplicity; BR(d) denotes: for all P, open U and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every such W, ∂R is integer multiplicity. Then for every d ∈ ℕ, CL(d) and BR(d) imply CL(d+1): for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), T is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part V, V1 (boundaries) and V2 (localization, Simon Ch. 6, Remark 8.3(1)), reducing CL(d+1) to the compact case (CL*) proved by the sibling dmcbr_closure_compact_support. The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the relevant parts of the frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) dimred_mbl_current_foundations (first conjunct), dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (mass identity), dimred_mbl_current_foundations (second conjunct), dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds, dimred_mbl_deformation_theorem, dtc_vanish_off_support. Siblings used: dmcbr_measure_convergence_tools ((T1), (T2), (MM)), dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (im_local), dmcbr_closure_compact_support (closure_compact). n := d + 1 ≥ 1; for currents of degree n, boundaryMassOn(X, W) = M_W(∂X).

Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T_j IM, Λ_W := sup_j(M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and T_j ⇀ T.
1. (V1) For each j, ∂T_j is IM by BR(d) (M_W(∂T_j) ≤ Λ_W < ∞). By lower semicontinuity (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf and WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), M_W(T) ≤ Λ_W and M_W(∂T) ≤ Λ_W for open W ⊂⊂ U; so T and ∂T have locally finite mass and (REP) gives admissible representations (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}).
2. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U; G := B_{r₀}(x₀) (open, G ⊂⊂ U). Let R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) and R'_j be IMReps of T_j and ∂T_j, μ_j := R_j.measure, μ'_j := R'_j.measure. By (MR), μ_j(W) = M_W(T_j) and μ'_j(W) = M_W(∂T_j) for open W, so sup_j(μ_j(K) + μ'_j(K)) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (K lies in some open W ⊂⊂ U); by (IMC)(d) the pairs (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ'_j, R'_j.orient) are admissible representations of T_j, ∂T_j.
3. (T1) applied to (μ_j) in U gives a subsequence (not relabeled; still T_j ⇀ T, still the bounds Λ_W) and a Borel measure μ with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U.
4. Slices. f := |· − x₀| (1-Lipschitz). For each j, (SL) for T_j with (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ'_j, R'_j.orient), f, L := 1 gives A_{j,t}(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j, B_{j,t}, and Z_{j,t} := ∂A_{j,t} − B_{j,t} with Z_{j,t}(η) = 0 when tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅ and M_G(Z_{j,t}) ≤ liminf_h h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}). (MM) with μs j := μ_j, G, (a, b) := (0, r₀), L := 1, Z_j(t) := M_G(Z_{j,t}) (μ_j(G ∩ {0 < f < r₀}) ≤ M_G(T_j) ≤ Λ_G) gives a measurable majorant with finite integral, so liminf_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞ for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀). Also μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0 for all but countably many r (μ is σ-finite). Fix r ∈ (0, r₀) with both properties and pass to a further subsequence with sup_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞.
5. Total slice mass. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in G and χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the sphere {f = r} (compact, ⊆ G as r < r₀). Then tsupport((1 − χ)ω) ∩ {f = r} = ∅, so Z_{j,r}((1 − χ)ω) = 0 and Z_{j,r}(ω) = Z_{j,r}(χω) ≤ M_G(Z_{j,r}) (χω is admissible for M_G). Hence M(Z_{j,r}) := M_U(Z_{j,r}) ≤ M_G(Z_{j,r}).
6. T'_j := A_{j,r} = T_j⌞B_r(x₀) is IM: (IMC)(b) with E := B_r(x₀) gives an IMRep (M_j ∩ B_r(x₀), θ_j, ξ_j) of a current whose values are ∫_{M_j∩B_r(x₀)}θ_jξ_j(ω)dH^n = A_{j,r}(ω). If tsupport ω ∩ B̄_r(x₀) = ∅ then T'_j(ω) = 0, so spt T'_j ⊆ K := B̄_r(x₀). M(T'_j) ≤ μ_j(B_r(x₀)) ≤ Λ_G, and ∂T'_j = B_{j,r} + Z_{j,r} with M(B_{j,r}) ≤ μ'_j(B_r(x₀)) ≤ Λ_G; so sup_j(M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j)) ≤ 2Λ_G + sup_jM_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞.
7. Convergence. Let A_r := T⌞B_r(x₀) be the current ω ↦ ∫_{f<r}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T (e.g. the first family of (SL) for T with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T})). (T2) (Xs := T_j with (μ_j, ξ_j); X := T with (μ_T, ξ_T); the limit μ of step 3, μ{f = r} = μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0; f continuous) gives T'_j(ω) → A_r(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
8. Extension to ℝ^P. Fix ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K. Define T̂'_j(ω) := T'_j(ζω) and Â_r(ω) := A_r(ζω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P); these are currents in ℝ^P (multiplication by ζ preserves test-form convergence and maps into 𝒟^n(U); more simply, for X ∈ {T'_j, A_r} with an admissible representation (μ_X, ξ_X), |X(ζω)| ≤ sup_x|ω(x)|·μ_X(tsupport ζ) < ∞, and test-form convergence ω_i → 0 forces sup_x|ω_i(x)| → 0, the Euclidean coefficient norm being bounded by a constant multiple of the operator norm of covectors). T̂'_j is IM: the IMRep (M_j ∩ B_r(x₀), θ_j, ξ_j), viewed in ℝ^P (Borel carrier, ∫_{M_j∩B_r∩K'}θ_j ≤ μ_j(K) < ∞ for every compact K'), represents it because ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀). spt T̂'_j ⊆ K, M(T̂'_j) ≤ M(T'_j) (ζω admissible when ω is). For η ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(ℝ^P), ∂T̂'_j(η) = T'_j(ζdη) and ∂T'_j(ζη) = T'_j(d(ζη)). The test form ζdη − d(ζη) ∈ 𝒟^n(U) vanishes on the open set N := interior{ζ = 1} ⊇ K (near every point of N, ζη = η, so d(ζη) = dη = ζdη there); hence its support lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ N, which is disjoint from spt T'_j ⊆ K, and (VO) gives T'_j(ζdη) = T'_j(d(ζη)) (no Leibniz rule for d is needed). Thus ∂T̂'_j(η) = ∂T'_j(ζη), and M(∂T̂'_j) ≤ M(∂T'_j) since |ζη| ≤ |η|. Hence sup_j(M(T̂'_j) + M(∂T̂'_j)) < ∞, and T̂'_j(ω) = T'_j(ζω) → A_r(ζω) = Â_r(ω): T̂'_j ⇀ Â_r in ℝ^P.
9. ∂T̂'_j is IM by BR(d) in U := ℝ^P (T̂'_j IM; M_W(∂T̂'_j) ≤ M(∂T'_j) < ∞ for every W).
10. By closure_compact (CL(d), BR(d), (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO); the compact set K, IM currents T̂'_j with IM boundaries, spt T̂'_j ⊆ K, bounded total masses, T̂'_j ⇀ Â_r), Â_r is IM.
11. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(B_r(x₀)): Â_r(ω) = A_r(ζω) = A_r(ω) = ∫_{B_r(x₀)}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = T(ω) (ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀), and ω vanishes off B_r(x₀)). So T|_{B_r(x₀)} = Â_r|_{B_r(x₀)}, which is IM by part (2) of im_local (in ℝ^P, V := B_r(x₀)). Since x₀ ∈ U was arbitrary (with some r > 0, B_r(x₀) ⊆ U) and T has locally finite mass (step 1), part (1) of im_local shows that T is IM. (If n > P all n-currents vanish and the argument still applies; T = 0 is IM.) ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂T_j IM by BR(d); T, ∂T have locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity).
IMRep measures of T_j converge on U along a subsequence (T1).
Slicing by |· − x₀| and (MM) give a radius r with bounded slice masses and μ(∂B_r) = 0.
T_j⌞B_r(x₀) are IM, supported in B̄_r(x₀), with bounded masses and boundary masses, and converge to T⌞B_r(x₀) (T2).
Extend to ℝ^P by a cutoff; boundaries are IM by BR(d); closure_compact makes the extended limit IM.
It agrees with T on B_r(x₀); im_local (2) then (1) shows T is IM.

audit.reason: Good-radius localization and cutoff extension satisfy every closure_compact hypothesis; BR(d) supplies the extended boundaries' integrality, and im_local returns CL(d+1). This localization agrees with [Simon §6.8.3](https://web.stanford.edu/class/math285/ts-gmt). The independently compiled induction establishes both frozen parent conjuncts.
